legalName: Segregation of Arrest Records After Acquittal, Dismissal or Withdrawal of Charges (KRS 17.142)
publicName: Ask agencies to file away the record of an arrest that went nowhere
mechanism: A law enforcement or other public agency holding arrest records, fingerprints, photographs or other data must, on the written request of the arrestee, segregate those records into a file separate from those of convicted persons where the person was found innocent or all charges relating to the offence were dismissed or withdrawn. The person may instead apply to the court, which shall forthwith issue an order to all law enforcement agencies. Each agency must notify every agency it shared the records with, and the segregated record must show the disposition. Records subject to KRS 431.076 or KRS 431.078 are sealed under those statutes instead.

rationale: The registry declares outputStrategyDeclared 'composed' with compositionMode 'alternative' and lists two units[], both marked available:true, both outputStrategy 'custom_pleading', both outputStrategyStatus 'resolved' and packetIdentity 'identified'.

The two units are genuinely alternative, not sequential: the registry destination detail states "The two routes are independent: either obtains segregation, and a participant may use both." The participant chooses via screening key segRoute.

No official form exists for either instrument. The registry records no officialFormId on any packetSet component and the unit description says in terms "No official form exists, so the application is drafted." There is therefore no official_form_dependency unit on this route and no lane-D/E blocker.

A third component, routing_guidance, is required by the registry packet set. It is carried as a participant_instruction unit because on an alternative-composition route the choice between the two instruments is itself the thing the participant must be walked through, and KRS 17.142(4) makes routing away from this track the common correct answer.

The route is drafted with an open build blocker recorded, not withheld: the blocker asks whether this should be a participant-facing relief track at all, not what the instruments would say. Nothing about the two instruments' vehicle, venue or content is unknown.

authoritySpine.description: A law enforcement or other public agency holding arrest records, fingerprints, photographs or other data must, on the written request of the arrestee, segregate those records into a file separate from those of convicted persons where the person was found innocent or all charges relating to the offence were dismissed or withdrawn.

The person may instead apply to the court, upon receipt of which the court shall forthwith issue an order to all law enforcement agencies. The subsection provides for an application to the court without stating a fee.

Each agency segregates the records into a file separate and apart from those of convicted persons, must notify every agency it shared the records with, and the segregated record must show the disposition of the case.

Records subject to the provisions of KRS 431.076 or 431.078 shall be sealed as provided in those statutes. This sends most acquittals and dismissals elsewhere and leaves withdrawn charges as the clearest residual use of this route.

authoritySpine.citation: Kentucky Circuit Court Clerks' Manual, July 2026 — Glossary, segregation code SG
authoritySpine.description: Court records are not records which may be segregated. This route reaches law enforcement and other public agency records only.

units.legalUnit: Apply to the court under KRS 17.142(2) for an order of segregation binding all law enforcement agencies
units.legalUnitSourceRef: registry@3b6f4c1:tracks[ky_criminal_record_segregation].units[0] (unitId ky_seg_court_application, verbatim label "Apply to the court for an order of segregation")

applicability.includedWhen: Screening answers "Do you want to apply to the court for one order covering every agency, or write directly to each agency, or both?" (segRoute) with the court route or with both. The registry unit description gives the reason to prefer it: on receipt the court shall forthwith issue an order to all law enforcement agencies, so one filing reaches every agency at once and carries the KRS 17.142(3) duty on each agency to notify everyone it passed the records to.
applicability.excludedWhen: segRoute answers agency-letters-only; or segAlreadyExpunged reports the records are already expunged or are eligible under KRS 431.076 or KRS 431.078, which KRS 17.142(4) sends to those statutes instead and which is a self-help stop condition; or the participant reports that fewer than all charges relating to the offence were dismissed or withdrawn.

units.notes: Corresponds to registry packetSet component ky_criminal_record_segregation-primary-filing-1 (role primary_filing, requirement conditional, conditionDescription "Applies on the court application unit."). No official form exists, so the application is drafted. KRS 17.142 provides for no notice to a prosecutor or any other party, and no service is required on this route, so the application carries no certificate of service.

units.legalUnit: Send a written request under KRS 17.142(1) to each law enforcement or other public agency holding the records
units.legalUnitSourceRef: registry@3b6f4c1:tracks[ky_criminal_record_segregation].units[1] (unitId ky_seg_agency_written_request, verbatim label "Send a written request to each agency holding the records")

applicability.includedWhen: Screening answers segRoute with the agency-letter route or with both. One letter is generated per agency the participant identifies in segAgencies. The statutory duty to segregate runs to the agency on the arrestee's written request without any court involvement.
applicability.excludedWhen: segRoute answers court-application-only; or segAgencies is empty, since the letters exist only per identified agency; or segAlreadyExpunged reports records already expunged or eligible under KRS 431.076 or KRS 431.078.

units.notes: Corresponds to registry packetSet component ky_criminal_record_segregation-agency-written-request-2 (role agency_written_request, requirement conditional, conditionDescription "Applies on the written-request unit, one letter per agency identified."). This unit is not a court document and is not filed anywhere; the participant posts each letter. No agency address is prefilled: the registry names no agency and no address for this track.

units.legalUnit: Decide, before either instrument is used, whether KRS 17.142(4) sends these records to KRS 431.076 or KRS 431.078 instead — and if not, which of the two segregation routes to use

counselFlags.statement: The controlling review classifies this slot as an agency-level mechanism retained for completeness and expressly NOT a product track, and supplies no output strategy, filing actor or destination. The current official text of KRS 17.142 contains two participant-initiated routes, one of which is a court application on which relief is mandatory, so the product rule points the other way. Normalizing it as a buildable relief track is a departure from the review. This route is therefore drafted as a container and marked blocked at the product-classification level; nothing about the instruments themselves is unknown.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: Should KRS 17.142 segregation be built as a participant-facing relief track, given that the statute contains two participant-initiated routes, notwithstanding the review's classification of it as not a product track?

counselFlags.statement: The static legal propositions BOTH generated instruments would assert about the effect of segregation — the KRS 17.142(3) segregation duty, the downstream duty on each agency to notify every agency it shared the records with, and the requirement that the segregated record show the disposition — have not been ratified.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: Ratify the fixed statements of legal effect the segregation application and the agency letters may make.

counselFlags.statement: Whether any court filing fee attaches to a KRS 17.142(2) application is unresolved. None was identified: the subsection provides for an application to the court without stating a fee, and the registry records fees as "none identified for either route". That is an absence of evidence, not evidence of absence. No fee figure and no no-fee promise is stated to any participant anywhere in this route; the participant instructions tell the participant to ask the clerk.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: Whether a filing fee attaches to a KRS 17.142(2) application, before any fee statement of either kind reaches a participant.

counselFlags.statement: KRS 17.142(4) sends records subject to KRS 431.076 or KRS 431.078 to those statutes instead. In practice that is most acquittals and dismissals, so segregation is a fallback. Records eligible under those statutes should be expunged rather than segregated because expungement is materially stronger, and that is a self-help stop condition. The clearest residual use of this route is charges withdrawn, which KRS 431.076 does not name.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That screening routes eligible records to the KRS 431.076 / KRS 431.078 expungement tracks before this route is ever offered, and that segAlreadyExpunged is a gate rather than a collected answer.

counselFlags.statement: Court records cannot be segregated. The Clerks' Manual glossary records that court records are not records which may be segregated. This route reaches law enforcement and other public agency records only, and neither instrument may ask a court to segregate its own record.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That the drafted application never requests segregation of court records, and that participant copy never implies the court file is reached.

counselFlags.statement: Segregation is not expungement. The records continue to exist and remain accessible; they are merely filed separately from those of convicted persons, and the segregated record must show the disposition. A participant who expects background checks to come back clean is a self-help stop condition.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That no participant copy or rendered output promises erasure, sealing, destruction or a clean background check.

counselFlags.statement: Whether ALL charges relating to the offence were dismissed or withdrawn is the statutory gate on KRS 17.142(1), and it is the participant's own statement of fact. Any dispute about it ends automated assistance. Neither instrument asserts a favourable-disposition conclusion of its own; both state the participant's own answer as the participant's own averment.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That no pipeline stage derives, infers or asserts that all charges relating to the offence ended favourably.

counselFlags.statement: No source read for this track names a single Kentucky record-holding agency or supplies any agency address. The agencies come only from the participant's own answer to segAgencies, and the letters name and address only what the participant supplies. No arresting agency, jail, state police division or records unit is prefilled anywhere on this route.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That agency identity and address reach the letters only through the participant's own screening answers.

counselFlags.statement: County, case number, court name, judge, prosecutor identity, prosecutor position, filing date and any agency response are blank in every fixture and are never prefilled. Case number is conditional in the registry's own generation requirements, because charges may never have been filed; the court application must work with it absent.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That the application renders correctly with no case number, since the venue on the no-charges-filed branch is the court where the case WOULD have been tried.

counselFlags.statement: KRS 17.142 provides for no notice to a prosecutor or any other party, and no service is required on the court route. No certificate of service is drafted for the application and no prosecutor is named on it. On the agency route the participant posts the letters and no proof of posting is drafted either.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That no service or notice step is added to the court application by local practice; confirm with the clerk before shipping.

counselFlags.statement: The two routes are independent: either obtains segregation, and a participant may use both. compositionMode is 'alternative', not 'sequential' — neither unit is a precondition of the other, and nothing in this route sequences them.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That screening presents the choice as genuinely alternative and permits both, matching segRoute's three answers.

counselFlags.statement: No official form exists for either instrument. The registry records no officialFormId on any of the three packetSet components and states in the unit description that "No official form exists, so the application is drafted." There is no lane-D/E official-form dependency on this route and nothing here is blocked on form acquisition.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That no Kentucky AOC form for a KRS 17.142(2) application has since been published; the Clerks' Manual glossary records segregation code SG but no form.

profilePassageReferenced.passage: The compiled KY profile enumerates five and only five pathways: 'Misdemeanor, violation, or traffic-infraction conviction expungement under KRS 431.078'; 'Eligible felony conviction vacatur and expungement under KRS 431.073'; 'Acquittal, dismissal, or failure-to-indict expungement under KRS 431.076'; 'Juvenile automatic expungement on qualifying dismissal'; and 'Juvenile petition to vacate and expunge under KRS 610.330'.
profilePassageReferenced.reading: The profile records NO unit, document, form or step for KRS 17.142 segregation — the strings '17.142' and 'segregat' do not occur anywhere in the 87 KB profile, and its source corpus (profile:source.allFolderFiles) is six expungement-side AOC PDFs, one PDF reference file and two HTML reference files. The profile therefore adds no unit to this route and omits none: it is silent on the mechanism. Its one relevant contribution is negative and is honoured here — KRS 431.076 and KRS 431.078 are live pathways in the profile, which is exactly where KRS 17.142(4) sends most of this route's candidate records, and unit 3 exists to make that routing happen before either instrument is produced.

Signature on the application and on each agency letter — a completion item on documents already enumerated, not a further unit.
Posting each agency letter, and addressing the envelopes — a completion item on unit 2, not a further unit.
